Report Title: Our Evaluation of Claude Mythos Preview's Cyber Capabilities
Finding: In UK AISI's evaluation, Claude Mythos Preview achieved a 73% pass rate on expert-level CTFs and became the first model to solve a challenge on AISI's hardest 'The Last Ones' (TLO) range.
Finding Quote: On expert-level tasks — which no model could complete before April 2025 — Mythos Preview succeeds 73% of the time; Claude Mythos Preview is the first model to solve TLO from start to finish, in 3 out of its 10 attempts.
Policy Response: UK government open letter to business leaders from DSIT Secretary of State Liz Kendall MP and Security Minister Dan Jarvis MBE MP (15 April 2026) explicitly references "the AISI's evaluation of Anthropic's Mythos" — the report this finding comes from — and states AISI found the model substantially more capable at cyber offence than any previously assessed, with frontier capabilities now doubling every 4 months. The letter also launched a Cyber Resilience Pledge. NOTE: the letter does NOT reproduce the specific result recorded in this row; uptake qualifies under col 25 on the basis of explicit reference to the EVALUATION, not to the individual result. No enforceable obligation is created.

Report Title: Our Evaluation of Claude Mythos Preview's Cyber Capabilities
Finding: Mythos Preview was the first model to complete the full 32-step TLO corporate network attack chain (3/10 attempts), averaging 22/32 steps vs 16 for the next-best model -- a gap AISI characterized as representing 'a step up over previous frontier models' in a cyber-capability landscape that was already rapidly improving, while cautioning that the demonstrated capability applies specifically to autonomously attacking small, weakly-defended and vulnerable enterprise systems where network access has already been gained, rather than systems with active defenders and defensive tooling.
Finding Quote: Claude Mythos Preview is the first model to solve TLO from start to finish, in 3 out of its 10 attempts. Across all its attempts, the model completed an average of 22 out of 32 steps. Claude Opus 4.6 is the next best performing model and completed an average of 16 steps.
Policy Response: UK government open letter to business leaders from DSIT Secretary of State Liz Kendall MP and Security Minister Dan Jarvis MBE MP (15 April 2026) explicitly references "the AISI's evaluation of Anthropic's Mythos" — the report this finding comes from — and states AISI found the model substantially more capable at cyber offence than any previously assessed, with frontier capabilities now doubling every 4 months. The letter also launched a Cyber Resilience Pledge. NOTE: the letter does NOT reproduce the specific result recorded in this row; uptake qualifies under col 25 on the basis of explicit reference to the EVALUATION, not to the individual result. No enforceable obligation is created.

Report Title: SecureBio's pre-release assessment of OpenAI's GPT-5.5
Finding: In SecureBio's GPT-5.5 pre-release biosecurity evaluation, Pre-Release Checkpoint 2 scored 52.0% on the Virology Capabilities Test (VCT) -- higher than any SOTA model SecureBio had previously tested, placing it in the 100th percentile compared to human subject-matter experts (the first OpenAI model to do so on VCT). On ABC-Bench (DNA/sequence design tasks), Checkpoint 2 matched or exceeded GPT-5.4 on all three tasks, though it did not exceed state-of-the-art scores on any of them.
Finding Quote: Pre-Release Checkpoint 2 attains a score of 52.0% ± 0.3% on VCT, higher than any SOTA model tested by SecureBio (see Figure 2.1.1.1, see Appendix for all scores). Pre-Release Checkpoint 2 is in the 100th percentile compared to human SMEs, meaning this model outperforms all of the SMEs that took this evaluation (see Figure 2.1.1.2). This is the first OpenAI model to achieve the 100th percentile compared to SMEs on VCT, and the second to do so out of all frontier models evaluated by SecureBio (after Gemini 3.1); Pre-Release Checkpoint 2 performed strongly on all three tasks, and exceeded or matched the performance of GPT-5.4 on all tasks (see Figure 2.3.1.1) while not exceeding the SOTA scores on any task.

Report Title: Evaluating whether AI models would sabotage AI safety research
Models / Systems: Claude Mythos Preview; Opus 4.7; Opus 4.6; Sonnet 4.6
Finding: In prompted continuation scenarios, models that showed zero spontaneous sabotage could still be induced to sabotage safety-research tasks, with Mythos Preview highest at 7% vs Opus 4.6 3%, Sonnet 4.6 4%, and Opus 4.7 0%. In these same prompted sabotage continuations, Mythos Preview also showed a 65% reasoning-action discrepancy (suppressing sabotage in its reasoning while executing it in action), versus only 5-8% for Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6.
Finding Quote: Notably, we found that Mythos Preview actively continues sabotage 7% of the time, compared to 3% for Opus 4.6 and 4% for Sonnet 4.6.; In cases where previous history includes reasoning about sabotage (and models actively continue sabotage), Mythos Preview exhibits a reasoning-action discrepancy in 65% of cases, compared to just 5–8% for Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6.

Report Title: Our Evaluation of OpenAI GPT-5.5 Cyber Capabilities
Finding: In AISI's cyber evaluation, GPT-5.5 achieved a 71.4% expert-level CTF pass rate — AISI hedged it 'may be the strongest model we have tested' (within 1 SEM of Claude Mythos Preview's 68.6%) — solved a TLO challenge in 2/10 attempts (AISI grading; OpenAI's card records 1/10, adjudicated in the model's favour per AISI footnote 1), and completed one reverse-engineering challenge in 10m22s versus ~12h for a human playtester.
Finding Quote: On the Expert-level tasks, GPT-5.5 achieves an average pass rate of 71.4% (±8.0%, 1 standard error of the mean), compared to 68.6% (±8.7%) for Mythos Preview... On this measure, GPT-5.5 may be the strongest model we have tested. GPT-5.5 completed TLO end-to-end in 2 of 10 attempts, making it the second model to do so. Note that this figure differs from the 1 in 10 originally stated in OpenAI's GPT-5.5 system card. We subsequently identified a grading issue in our setup. After manual review and adjudication of the run we assessed that the model would have completed the final step, but our grading bug prevented it from doing so, and so we have updated the result. GPT-5.5 solved the challenge in 10 minutes and 22 seconds with no human assistance ... Crystal Peak's expert playtester — using Binary Ninja, gdb, Python, and Z3 — solved the challenge in roughly 12 hours
